t: Maximum Sum of an Hourglass — Direct Scan
o: An hourglass is a 3×3 block with the middle-left and middle-right cells removed. With m,n <= 150 there are at most ~148×148 ≈ 22k hourglasses, each needing 7 additions — brute force is trivially fast. Example 2: the only hourglass in a 3×3 grid sums 1+2+3+5+7+8+9 = 35. Constraints signal that no clever algorithm is required; correctness of the cell selection is the only challenge.
k: Enumerate top-left corners (i,j) with i+2<m and j+2<n.
Sum = row i (3 cells) + grid[i+1][j+1] + row i+2 (3 cells).
Prefix sums are unnecessary at these sizes but would give O(mn) with tiny constants.

a.i: Slide a 3×3 frame over the grid; for each valid top-left corner add the three top cells, the center cell, and the three bottom cells, skipping the middle-row sides. Track the maximum. Grid values are non-negative so initializing the answer to 0 is safe.
s: Loop i from 0 to m-3, j from 0 to n-3.
Keep the running maximum and return it.
a.t: O(m·n) — constant work (7 additions) per hourglass position.

w: The only real pitfalls are misreading the hourglass shape (excluding the wrong cells) and loop bounds (must leave room for 3 rows/columns). If asked to optimize for huge grids, present a 2D prefix-sum variant: hourglass sum = 3×3 box sum − middle-left − middle-right, answered in O(1) per position after O(mn) preprocessing.
